topic: Where did the money go, not why: a calm 20-minute look at last month's spending, sorted into simple piles without judgment
pillar: STARTING OVER: the feelings and the small first moves (the 2 A.M. math, 'where did the money go, not why', permission to go slowly).
caption:
Where did the money go? That is the only question for today.
Open your bank app, take the last 30 days, and give each spend a one-word label.
Group them into a few piles, add them up roughly, and stop when 20 minutes are up.
Save this for a quiet hour this week.
If you want one page to write it all down, the free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is at the link in bio.
Day one counts.

General education, not financial advice.

#lifeafterdivorce #startingover #moneybasics #divorcedwomen #financialfirststeps

slides.title: You are allowed to just look
slides.body: Before budgets or big plans, there is one small move. Look at where your money went last month. The why can wait.

slides.title: What you need
items: Your bank app or last month's statement
A notebook or a notes app

slides.title: The 20-minute look
items: Pick one account and the last 30 days
Give each spend a one-word label: food, gas, home, phone
Group the labels into 5 or 6 simple piles
Add up each pile. Rough numbers are fine.
Stop when the timer ends, even if you are not done

slides.title: Leave the why in the margin
slides.body: If a thought starts with the words I should not have, jot it in the margin and keep going. Today you are collecting facts. Facts are calm. They do not need you to defend them.

slides.title: This becomes one of your Three Numbers
slides.body: Those piles show you what goes out. Once you can see it, the next steps feel less scary. You do not have to decide or change anything today. Seeing is enough.

slides.title: Keep this for a quiet hour
slides.body: Want one page to write your piles on? The free Three Numbers Starter Sheet is made for this. You can grab it through the link in bio. Day one counts.
